recipes.title: Database performance baseline monitoring

description.need: A database degrades against its own normal long before it crosses any generic threshold, so a team watching fixed numbers either misses the degradation or is trained by false alarms to ignore the ones that matter.
description.input: Metric samples read from one database at a regular interval, the baseline learned from earlier samples, and the operator's past verdicts on which patterns turned out to be nothing.
description.core_action: Judge each sample against what this database actually does at this hour of this day, and decide whether a move is worth a glance, worth waking someone, or worth nothing at all.
description.output: A per metric baseline that survives a restart, and alerts that name the baseline they departed from and by how far.

activities.label: Read the configured metrics from the database at a regular interval
Extend the per metric and per hour baseline with the new samples
Judge each metric against its own learned normal rather than a fixed threshold
Separate a move worth a glance from a breach worth waking someone
Raise the breach naming the baseline it left and by how much

outcomes.statement: Deviation is judged against what this database actually does, not against a generic threshold.
success_criteria: An alert names the baseline it deviated from and by how much
A metric still inside its learning period is reported as unjudged rather than alerted on
A pattern the operator repeatedly calls a false positive gets quieter without being switched off

outcomes.statement: Losing sight of the database is itself reported.
success_criteria: Repeated collection failures produce a message rather than silence
A gap in sampling is visible in the record so the baseline is not trusted more than it deserves

recipes.guidance: Own the answer to whether this database is behaving like itself. Alert on deviation from its own learned normal and hold the line that quiet means measured and healthy, never unmeasured. A single spike rarely deserves a message; a sustained move, or several metrics moving together, usually does. Say what changed and how far from normal it went, and leave the remedy to the operator's decision.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A baseline exists only if the same metrics are sampled at a regular interval, so a gap in sampling is a hole in the baseline rather than a missed report. The interval should match how fast this database can actually degrade.

personalization_needs: Which database, which engine, and which read only credential, because the metrics worth collecting differ per engine and this work must never hold a write credential
What this operator would want to be woken for, because the line between a warning and a critical is a judgement about his tolerance rather than a statistical fact
Which periods are known to be abnormal by design, such as a nightly batch, because otherwise the baseline learns the batch as an anomaly and alerts on it forever

input_schema.name: baseline_days
input_schema.description: Silent learning period before alerts are enabled.

input_schema.name: metrics_scope
options: Full (response time, throughput, connections, locks, cache, disk I/O)
input_schema.description: Which dimensions to track and threshold.

input_schema.name: warning_multiplier
input_schema.description: Stddev multiplier for warning-level alerts.

input_schema.name: critical_multiplier
input_schema.description: Stddev multiplier for critical escalation. Must be > warning_multiplier.

input_schema.name: rolling_window_minutes
input_schema.description: Sliding window used to smooth momentary spikes.

recipes.title: Database health check

description.need: A connection pool filling up, a slow query count climbing, or replication falling behind is a performance indicator for days before it is an outage, and nobody looks until it is the outage.
description.input: Read only health queries against one database, plus the rolling record of what those same queries returned on earlier passes.
description.core_action: Compare each health signal against its own recent history rather than a fixed number, and decide which movements are worth reporting and which are the database working normally.
description.output: A health account naming what moved, against what history, and an explicit Critical when the database could not be reached at all.

activities.label: Run the read only health queries the engine supports
Compare each signal against its own rolling history
Decide which movements are worth someone's attention
Report the account, with unreachability raised as its own Critical
Extend the rolling history so the next pass has something to compare against

outcomes.statement: A degrading connection pool, growing slow query count, or replication lag is known while it is still a performance indicator, not after it becomes an outage.
success_criteria: Every check compares current metrics against the rolling baseline, not a static number.
Database unreachability is always surfaced as its own Critical incident, never folded silently into a generic failure.

recipes.guidance: Own catching database degradation early enough that it never becomes a surprise outage. Run read only health checks against connection pool, slow queries, table growth, replication lag, bloat, and failed migrations, and compare each against its own rolling baseline rather than a fixed number. Unreachability is always Critical and always surfaced prominently. A permission gap is a credential issue to flag, not a reason to fail silently.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Nothing outside obliges this pass and no baseline depends on its regularity, unlike the sampling that feeds performance monitoring. Look when the database has changed enough to be worth re reading, or when a signal reported last time should now be verifiably better or worse.

personalization_needs: Which database and which engine, because the health queries that exist at all differ per engine
Which read only credential this work holds, because a health check must never be able to write
What the adopter already knows to be abnormal by design, such as a table that grows fast on purpose, so it is not reported as a finding every pass

recipes.title: Infrastructure metrics scan

description.need: Infrastructure usually fails by drifting away from its own recent normal, not by crossing a memorable round number, so a watch built on absolute thresholds sees the failure late or not at all.
description.input: CPU, memory, error rate, latency percentile and availability read from the monitoring provider, the rolling baseline for each, and what earlier triage decided about which deviations were noise.
description.core_action: Compare each metric against its own baseline instead of a shared static threshold, and let past triage decisions decide how loudly a familiar deviation is reported.
description.output: An infrastructure section naming which metrics left their own normal, with the provider's unavailability stated plainly rather than shown as an absence of findings.

activities.label: Pull the configured metrics from the monitoring provider
Compare each metric against its own rolling baseline
Damp deviations that past triage has already called noise
Contribute the infrastructure account, naming any section that could not be read

outcomes.statement: An infrastructure metric drifting from its own normal is caught even when it never crosses some universal red line.
success_criteria: CPU, memory, error rate, latency, and availability are each compared against their own rolling baseline, not a shared static threshold.
A corrupted baseline file is regenerated rather than left to silently produce false anomalies.

recipes.guidance: Own noticing when infrastructure is behaving differently from its own recent normal, not just when it crosses a scary looking absolute number. Compare each metric to its rolling baseline, and lean on what past triage has taught about which deviations turned out to be noise. When the monitoring provider is unreachable, say so plainly in the combined briefing rather than silently omitting the section.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The provider is already sampling continuously, so this work is a read of someone else's series rather than the sampler itself, and its regularity buys nothing the baseline needs. Look when the last read has aged past the rate at which this infrastructure changes, or when another signal suggests something moved.

personalization_needs: Which services or hosts count, because a baseline computed over everything hides the drift of the one thing that matters
What the adopter has already decided is noise, such as a CPU band that is normal here, since the same deviation is a finding in one operation and background in another
Where the account is read, because an infrastructure section that reaches nobody is the same as no scan

input_schema.name: lookback_hours
input_schema.description: Scan window for infrastructure metrics.

This is a real adoption hazard for a type this broad and is recorded as a lane finding rather than papered over with a narrower type that does not exist in the catalog.

recipes.title: Deploy regression correlation

description.need: When errors jump, whoever is on call starts from zero on the question that matters most, which is what changed just before, and the answer is sitting in the deploy list nobody cross referenced.
description.input: The deployment list for the window, the error rate series over the same window, and the size of correlation window the adopter considers meaningful.
description.core_action: Decide which error jumps are close enough to a deploy to be named as its regression, and which are merely near it in time and must be labelled as no more than possibly related.
description.output: Named regressions carrying the commit, the author and a rollback hint, and a clean statement when no deploy in the window explains anything.

activities.label: List the deployments that landed inside the window
Line the deploy times up against the error rate series
Decide which pairings are close enough to be called regressions
Name each regression with its commit, author and rollback hint, and soften the weak ones

outcomes.statement: When errors spike shortly after a deploy, whoever is on call already has the commit and author in hand instead of starting from zero.
success_criteria: A deploy within the configured correlation window of an error rate jump is named with commit SHA, author, and a rollback hint.
A weak or distant correlation is labeled 'possibly related' rather than asserted as a regression.

recipes.guidance: Own connecting error spikes back to the deploy that likely caused them, without crying wolf on coincidence. Cross reference deploy timestamps against error rate jumps within the configured window, and be explicit about confidence: a close in time correlation earns the regression label, a loose one gets a softer possibly related framing. No deploys in the window is a clean result to report, not a gap to fill with speculation.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A deploy is a real external event but the answer does not exist at the moment it lands, because the error series needs time to show the effect. Look once a recent deploy has had that time, or when an error jump is sitting unexplained.

personalization_needs: Where deploys are recorded here, because a platform deploy list, a tag history and a CI run log are three different sources with three different truths
How close in time counts as related in this operation, since the answer depends on how fast this system's users hit new code
Whether a named regression should reach a person immediately or wait for the next account

input_schema.name: correlation_window_hours
input_schema.description: How close a deploy must be to an error spike to count as regression-class.

recipes.title: Database anomaly baseline refresh

description.need: Anomaly detection is only as honest as the baseline behind it, and a baseline computed once quietly turns every ordinary business change into an anomaly and every real anomaly into normal.
description.input: A recent window of the database's own rows, the baseline currently in force, and knowledge of which past periods were abnormal by design.
description.core_action: Recompute the distributions detection depends on from what the business has actually been doing recently, and decide whether the new numbers are trustworthy enough to replace the old ones.
description.output: A current baseline in force, or the previous baseline still intact together with a plain statement that the refresh did not succeed.

activities.label: Read a recent window of the tables detection depends on
Recompute the per field distributions and rates
Decide whether the new numbers are trustworthy enough to replace the old
Install the new baseline, or keep the last good one and say the refresh failed

outcomes.statement: Anomaly detection is always judged against a baseline that reflects the business's actual recent behavior, not a stale snapshot.
success_criteria: Baselines are recalculated from a rolling recent window rather than a fixed one.
A failed refresh leaves the previous baseline intact rather than corrupting detection with a bad recalculation.

outcomes.statement: The state of each connected database is known to its owner, and what is wrong with it is written down where work gets picked up.
success_criteria: Every registered database connector has been read recently enough that its account is still true
Findings arrive with the table, the pattern, and why it matters, not as a metric dump
A finding already filed and still open is not filed again

recipes.guidance: Keep the numbers detection rests on honest as the business itself shifts, recomputing from a rolling recent window rather than a fixed one. Never let a failed refresh silently degrade detection: retain the last good baseline and say plainly that the refresh failed. Recover from a corrupted baseline by reinitialising rather than propagating bad numbers forward, and treat a distribution that has moved a long way as a finding in its own right.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A recompute over a trailing window is not a sampling obligation the way metric collection is, because the rows are already there whenever it runs. Act when a connector has gone unread for longer than its rate of change justifies, or when the anomaly watch has raised the same pattern more than once.

personalization_needs: Which databases this work owns and which are read only to it, because the answer changes what it may propose
What normal looks like for this data, since the adopter knows which spikes are the business working correctly
Whether findings should become backlog items automatically or be reported first

recipes.title: Database activity digest

description.need: A team that only ever sees individual database events has no sense of direction, and cannot tell a bad week from a normal one until something breaks.
description.input: Counts and records across the monitored tables for the period, the same counts for the previous period, and the anomaly log covering both.
description.core_action: Turn the period's activity into one account that shows direction of change rather than a table of totals, and decide what a reader would actually act on.
description.output: One digest covering the monitored tables with movement against the previous period, published even when a source was empty.

activities.label: Gather the period's activity across the monitored tables
Compare against the previous period to get direction, not just totals
Decide what a reader would actually act on
Publish the digest, reporting an empty source as zero rather than skipping

outcomes.statement: The team gets one read on database activity across the monitored tables, with movement against the previous period.
success_criteria: A digest covers each monitored table and anomalies by severity, with deltas from the prior period.
Missing anomaly logs still produce a digest reporting zero, rather than failing to post.

outcomes.statement: What is wrong with the database is written down where work gets picked up, not only described in a digest.
success_criteria: Findings arrive with the table, the pattern, and why it matters, not as a metric dump
A finding already filed and still open is not filed again

recipes.guidance: Compile the period's activity across every monitored table into one account that shows not just totals but direction of change. Treat a missing or empty log as a zero, not a reason to skip. Judgement here is deciding what is worth someone's attention rather than relaying everything measured, and anything that suggests data loss is escalated rather than filed as a line in a digest.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 Monday 09:00 cron is a delivery preference the adopter can restore on the charter. Act when a connector has gone unread for longer than its rate of change justifies, and remember that an adopter who genuinely wants a fixed morning digest can bind a time trigger without the recipe assuming one.

personalization_needs: Which tables carry consequences and which are noise, since a digest over everything equally is the same as a digest over nothing
Who reads this and what they are accountable for, because that decides which movements belong in it
Where the digest lands, given the adopter may have no external channel configured at all

recipes.title: Database row change watch

description.need: Row level change streams are almost entirely the product working correctly, so a watch that relays them all trains its audience to ignore it and hides the few changes that should never have happened.
description.input: Row change events from the watched tables, whatever context can be fetched about the affected record, and what this data normally does.
description.core_action: Judge which changes are genuinely off against what this data normally does, and decide who, if anyone, needs to hear about each one and in how much detail.
description.output: Quiet on routine volume, and for the rest an account carrying the record and the reason, with a burst collapsed into one message rather than many.

activities.label: Receive the row change and identify the table and operation
Fetch enough context about the affected record to judge it
Decide whether the change is routine or genuinely off
Decide who needs to hear it and at what depth of detail
Deliver once per change, collapsing a burst into a single account

outcomes.statement: A row change that should not have happened is noticed while it still matters.
success_criteria: Changes that break an invariant are surfaced with the record and the reason, not just a count
Routine volume produces no notification at all
A burst of related changes arrives as one account rather than one message per row

outcomes.statement: Every meaningful event reaches the right audience exactly once, with duplicates suppressed rather than relayed.
success_criteria: A repeated delivery of the same underlying change produces no second notification
A malformed payload is logged and skipped rather than failing silently

recipes.guidance: React to row level changes on the watched tables and judge which of them are genuinely off. Most changes are the product working, so the job is to be quiet about those and clear about the rest. Compare against what this data normally does rather than a fixed threshold, and collapse a flood into a single summary instead of relaying it. Escalate anything that reads as corruption or unauthorised change immediately.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A row changing is a real external event and the judgement is only useful while the change is recent, so this work wakes on arrival rather than choosing its own moment.

personalization_needs: Which tables carry consequences and which are noise, since watching everything equally is the same as watching nothing
What the adopter wants to be interrupted for versus what can wait for the periodic health read
Where an alert should land, given the adopter may have no channel configured at all

input_schema.name: channel_routing
input_schema.description: How to route messaging notifications. separate_by_type uses distinct channels per event kind; separate_by_severity routes by LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL; single_ops_channel funnels everything into one; team_specific maps to growth / engineering / ops.

input_schema.name: anomaly_sensitivity
input_schema.description: Order-value anomaly multiplier. Strict: >2× mean. Moderate: >3× mean. Loose: >5× mean. Disabled turns the detector off.

input_schema.name: enrichment_depth
input_schema.description: Notification detail. Minimal: event + table + timestamp. Standard: + key fields. Rich: full enriched payload. Adaptive: brief for routine events, rich for anomalies.

recipes.title: Database anomaly incident diagnosis

description.need: A serious database deviation reaches a person as an alarm and nothing else, so the first hour goes into reconstructing evidence that has already stopped existing.
description.input: The live state of the database while the condition is still happening, the metrics that moved alongside it, and the operator's verdicts on earlier hypotheses of the same shape.
description.core_action: Capture the evidence while it is still there, correlate what moved together, and offer a hypothesis carrying the confidence it actually deserves rather than the confidence that would be reassuring.
description.output: An escalation carrying evidence, a named hypothesis with its confidence and what would confirm or refute it, and remediation options with their costs.

activities.label: Capture the database's live state while the condition is still happening
Find the metrics that moved together with it
Name a root cause hypothesis and the confidence it deserves
Set out the remediation options and what each would cost
Escalate to a person, changing nothing on the database
Record the operator's verdict so the next case of this shape is judged with it

outcomes.statement: When something serious happens the operator gets evidence and a named hypothesis, not just an alarm.
success_criteria: Evidence is captured while the condition is live rather than reconstructed afterwards
The hypothesis states its confidence and what would confirm or refute it
A verdict from the operator changes how the next similar case is judged

outcomes.statement: What the human decided about an incident, true positive, false positive, or actual root cause, feeds back into how future anomalies are judged.
success_criteria: Every incident's triage outcome is persisted.
A recurring root cause becomes visible across incidents rather than being re-diagnosed from scratch each time.

recipes.guidance: Own the first honest explanation of a serious deviation. Capture what the database was doing while it is still doing it, correlate the metrics that moved together, and offer a hypothesis carrying the confidence it actually deserves. Do not act on the database to fix it. Name the options and what each would cost, and say plainly when the evidence supports no hypothesis at all.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A critical deviation is a real event and diagnosis has to begin while the evidence still exists, so this work wakes on the detection rather than choosing its own moment.

personalization_needs: What this work is allowed to touch during an incident, which is normally nothing, because the default has to be read only and the adopter should have to say otherwise explicitly rather than discover it
Who to reach and how when the operator is not the responder, because a diagnosis that reaches nobody in time is the same as no diagnosis
Which earlier incidents count as the same shape, since that is what turns a verdict into a lesson rather than a note

input_schema.name: require_review
input_schema.description: When true, critical incidents require human acknowledgment before automated response proceeds.

recipes.title: Incident capture and classification

description.need: One event usually gets reported several times by several people, and severity gets argued down once the pressure passes, so the record of what happened stops matching what happened.
description.input: An incoming report or automated signal, the set of incidents already open, and the severity language this team already uses.
description.core_action: Decide whether this is a new incident or another report of one already open, and set severity from impact on real users or real work rather than from the tone of the report.
description.output: One record per event, carrying an honest severity, an escalation expectation, and a timeline that stays readable afterwards.

activities.label: Take the report with enough detail to be judged
Check it against the incidents already open
Set severity from impact on real users or real work
Create or join the record with its escalation expectation
Tell whoever the severity says should know

outcomes.statement: Every incident has one honest record from first report through to closure.
success_criteria: Two reports of the same event become one record rather than two
Severity reflects impact and is set at intake rather than negotiated down afterwards
A closure is confirmed by a person rather than inferred from silence

outcomes.statement: An uncertain duplicate is resolved by a person rather than guessed at.
success_criteria: A likely duplicate is caught and resolved, merged or kept distinct, rather than silently creating a second incident for the same problem

recipes.guidance: Own the truth of the record. Duplicate reports of one event are the normal case, so join rather than fork. Set severity from impact on real users or real work, not from the tone of the report, and resist the quiet downgrade once the pressure passes. Close only when someone confirms it is actually over, and keep the timeline readable afterwards as what happened rather than what was tidied.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A report or an automated signal is a real external event, and the record has to be true at the moment someone reads it, so this work wakes on arrival rather than pacing itself.

personalization_needs: What counts as an incident in this operation, because too wide and the log becomes a task list, too narrow and the real ones are handled off the record
The severity language the operator already uses, because imposing a new scale means the record and the conversation about it stop matching
Who should hear about a serious one and how, because severity only matters if it changes who finds out

recipes.title: Open incident vigilance and escalation

description.need: Incidents are rarely abandoned deliberately; they go quiet, and without something watching the quiet a serious one sits untouched while a trivial one stays open forever.
description.input: The open incident set with, for each one, its severity, when it was last touched, and the nudges already sent about it.
description.core_action: Decide from the state of the board itself which incidents have been silent longer than their severity allows, and escalate with growing force rather than repeating the same nudge.
description.output: An open set where nothing serious is quietly abandoned, escalations that grew rather than repeated, and minor items closed with the reason they went away.

activities.label: Read the open set with each incident's last touch and its expectation
Decide which have been silent longer than their severity allows
Escalate with more force than the last nudge, not the same one again
Close a minor item that has genuinely gone away, with that reason recorded
Take a resolution to a person for closure confirmation rather than inferring it

outcomes.statement: An incident never goes quiet without someone noticing.
success_criteria: Every open incident has a last touched time and an expectation for its next update
Silence past that expectation produces a nudge or an escalation rather than a longer silence
A minor item that has genuinely gone away is closed with that reason rather than left open forever

outcomes.statement: An incident is never marked resolved on this work's own say so.
success_criteria: Resolution always waits on a person confirming closure
A gap in escalation coverage after a restart is caught and sent late with the real delay labeled, not pretended away

recipes.guidance: Own the open set between updates. What matters is not a fixed sweep but that nothing serious is quietly abandoned, and the expectation for how often an incident should be touched scales with its severity. Escalate on silence rather than on elapsed time alone, and watch that repeated nudges do not become noise a responder learns to ignore.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Decide when to look from the state of the board itself: a serious incident with no update needs attention far sooner than a minor one, and an empty board needs none at all. The v2 fifteen minute sweep spent the same effort on an empty board as on a full one.

personalization_needs: How often an incident of each severity should be touched here, because this is the only threshold the work rests on and it is a property of the team rather than a default
Who an escalation should reach at each step, since escalation that grows in force has to grow towards someone
What counts as a minor item that may be closed for going quiet, because that judgement differs sharply between operations

input_schema.name: auto_escalate_s1_minutes
input_schema.description: Minutes of no update before an S1 auto-escalates. Lower = faster response, higher alert fatigue.

recipes.title: Post-incident review and prevention proposals

description.need: The only lasting product of an incident is what was learned from it, and that evaporates within days unless somebody writes it while responders can still correct it.
description.input: A resolved incident with its timeline and resolution notes, and the record of causes behind earlier incidents.
description.core_action: Write an honest account of what happened, preferring a stated unknown cause to a plausible invented one, and decide when a cause has returned often enough that another review is the wrong response.
description.output: An account with timeline, impact, cause and specific action items, approved by a person, plus a prevention proposal where a cause keeps returning.

activities.label: Wait until responders are out of the fire but can still remember it
Reconstruct the timeline, impact and response from the record
Name a root cause or state plainly that it is unknown
Check the cause against earlier incidents and decide whether it is recurring
Turn a recurring cause into prevention work sized to be accepted or declined
Take the account to a person before it becomes the permanent record

outcomes.statement: A serious incident produces an honest account of what happened and what would stop it happening again.
success_criteria: The account names a root cause or states plainly that it is unknown
Action items are specific enough to be picked up as work
The account is written while responders can still correct it

outcomes.statement: Recurring causes are named as patterns rather than rediscovered each time.
success_criteria: An incident matching an earlier cause is linked to it
A cause that keeps returning is proposed as prevention work instead of reviewed again

recipes.guidance: Own the learning, which is the only lasting product of an incident. Write the account once responders are out of the fire but can still remember it. Prefer a stated unknown cause to a plausible invented one. Where the same cause keeps returning, stop writing reviews about it and propose the change that would end it, sized as work the operator can accept or decline.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Act when a resolved incident has settled enough that the account will be accurate, and separately when the record shows one cause recurring. The v2 recipe fired on resolution and then waited a fixed delay, which is a self paced judgement wearing an event's clothes.

personalization_needs: Which severities deserve a written account at all, because writing one for everything guarantees none of them are read
Where prevention proposals should go so they become real work, because a proposal that lands nowhere is the reason the same incident recurs
How long this team needs before an account will be accurate, since the right settling period is a property of how they work

input_schema.name: postmortem_delay_hours
input_schema.description: How long to wait after resolution before generating the review. Gives responders time to add final notes.

recipes.title: Application error scan

description.need: An error list that shows the same dismissed pattern every day teaches its readers to skim, and the one new error that matters goes past unread with the rest.
description.input: Unresolved errors from the monitoring provider over a window, and the record of how this team triaged patterns like them before.
description.core_action: Classify each error's severity from the data and from the triage history together, so a signature dismissed repeatedly quietly drops without anyone having to dismiss it again.
description.output: An error account holding what is genuinely new or escalating, with a degraded provider stated rather than reported as an all clear.

activities.label: Pull unresolved errors for the window from the provider
Match each against how patterns like it were triaged before
Set severity from the data and the triage history together
Separate genuinely new or escalating errors from familiar noise
Contribute the account, naming a degraded provider rather than implying an all clear

outcomes.statement: The team's attention goes to errors that are actually new or actually escalating, not the same dismissed pattern every day.
success_criteria: An error pattern dismissed as noise three or more times is auto-classified Low on future runs without needing a human to repeat the call.
Every Critical finding reaches the combined briefing regardless of monitoring-provider hiccups, via cached data if needed.

recipes.guidance: Own separating genuinely actionable errors from recurring noise, learning from how the team has triaged similar patterns before. Classify severity using both current data and the triage history, and let repeated dismissals of the same signature quietly lower its future severity. When the monitoring provider is degraded, fall back to the last good snapshot rather than reporting a false all clear.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The provider is already collecting continuously; this is a read of its series, and nothing outside obliges it at a particular hour. Look when enough has accumulated to be worth reading, or when something else suggests the error rate has moved.

personalization_needs: Which projects or services this scan is accountable for, because a provider account usually spans more than one team
What this team already treats as noise, since the same signature is a finding in one operation and background in another
How much a person can absorb per pass, which sets the severity floor rather than a default doing it

recipes.title: Production error issue filter

description.need: Root cause analysis is expensive per issue, so anything that reaches it must be worth investigating; a filter that passes everything makes the analysis step useless.
description.input: Unresolved issues from the error monitor for the scoped projects and window, their occurrence counts, and the record of which patterns have been dismissed as noise.
description.core_action: Apply the occurrence floor and the learned noise patterns to decide which issues are worth an investigation, without forming an opinion about what caused them.
description.output: A qualified set handed to root cause analysis, or a brief all clear when nothing qualifies.

activities.label: Query unresolved issues for the scoped projects and window
Drop issues below the occurrence floor
Suppress patterns dismissed as noise often enough to have earned it
Hand the qualified set on, or report a brief all clear

outcomes.statement: The root cause step only ever sees issues worth investigating, because known noise patterns are filtered before they get there.
success_criteria: An issue below the severity threshold or matching a known-noise pattern is not forwarded.
Three or more noise dismissals of a pattern measurably suppress it going forward.

recipes.guidance: Pull unresolved issues for the window and hand only the ones worth investigating to root cause analysis: apply the occurrence floor and let memory of past noise dismissals suppress patterns that keep turning out to be nothing. This is a filter, not a diagnosis, so it should never editorialise about cause.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Nothing outside obliges the filter to run at a given hour; it should run when enough unread issues have accumulated to make the pass worthwhile, and not at all when they have not.

personalization_needs: Which projects and which environment this filter covers, because a monitor account almost always spans more than the system in question
What counts as enough occurrences to be worth investigating here, since the floor is the whole filter
What the adopter has already dismissed as noise, so the filter starts from their history rather than from nothing

input_schema.name: severity_threshold
input_schema.description: Minimum occurrence count to surface an issue. Below = skipped.

recipes.title: Source-grounded error root cause analysis

description.need: A root cause report written from the stack trace alone restates what the reader already has, and the person triaging still has to open the code themselves.
description.input: One qualified issue with its latest event and stack trace, the source at the error location across the codebases in scope, and the callers that reach it.
description.core_action: Read the actual code at the error location, trace who calls it, and decide which of several plausible causes the evidence supports, ranking the resolutions by what each would cost.
description.output: A report per issue with a grounded cause, ranked resolutions, and an explicit statement wherever the source or the trace could not be reached.

activities.label: Fetch the latest event and its full stack trace
Read the source at the error location and trace its callers
Decide which cause the evidence actually supports
Rank the resolutions by what each would cost
Deliver one report per issue, naming every limitation it ran into

outcomes.statement: Whoever triages a qualified issue gets a real root cause hypothesis grounded in the actual source at the error location, not a restatement of the stack trace.
success_criteria: Every qualified issue produces a report with ranked resolutions at the configured depth.
When source cannot be found in any scoped codebase or the trace is unusable, the report says so plainly rather than fabricating a location.

recipes.guidance: Own turning a qualified issue into a root cause report a human can triage quickly, reading the actual code at the error location and tracing cross project callers rather than reasoning from the trace alone. Degrade gracefully when the source is offline, minified, or missing, always naming the limitation in the report. Every report goes to human triage; let their actionable versus noise decisions build the pattern library that sharpens future filtering.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A qualified issue arriving from the filter is a real event and the analysis exists only in response to it, so this work wakes on arrival rather than sweeping for issues itself.

personalization_needs: Which codebases the traces can land in, because a search across everything produces coincidental matches and that is what makes a grounded report untrustworthy
Whether the deployed code is minified or otherwise unmappable, since that decides whether source grounding is possible at all
What shape of report the triager actually reads, because depth beyond that is cost without value

recipes.title: Agent platform error ingestion

description.need: Some agent failures announce themselves and some just stop, and a record built only from the announcements is missing exactly the failures nobody noticed.
description.input: Failure events emitted by running agents, and the execution history that has to be sampled to find the failures that emitted nothing.
description.core_action: Catch failures both ways at once and normalise them into one record shape, deciding what is genuinely a repeat of something already recorded rather than a second failure.
description.output: One searchable error record covering announced and silent failures alike, with duplicates collapsed and a retention horizon that holds.

activities.label: Take failures from the events agents emit
Sample execution history for the failures that emitted nothing
Reduce both sources to one record shape
Decide what is a repeat rather than a second failure
Append to the record everything downstream reads from

outcomes.statement: Every agent failure, including a silent one no event ever announced, ends up in the same searchable error record.
success_criteria: Both event driven failures and polled silent failures land in the same index.
A duplicate within the dedup window does not create a second record.

recipes.guidance: Catch every agent failure two ways at once, by subscribing to error events and by sampling for the silent failures that never emit one, then normalise both into the same structured record. Deduplicate close together in time so one incident does not look like several. This is the ingestion layer other work builds classification and reporting on top of, so it should add no judgement of its own beyond what is a repeat.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A silent failure emits nothing, so the only thing that finds it is regular sampling, and a gap in the sampling is a hole in the record rather than a late report. This is the same argument that makes baseline collection a time obligation, and it is the reason this recipe keeps a time recommendation where the other digest and scan recipes in this lane lost theirs.

personalization_needs: How long the record must reach back, because retention is what downstream reporting can compare against
Which agents or workspaces are in scope, since an operator running several may not want them in one index
How close in time two failures have to be to count as the same one, which differs with how the agents are triggered

input_schema.description: How many days of error history to retain in `error_index.json`.

recipes.title: Agent platform error classification

description.need: A raw failure record tells nobody what to do, and a forced classification into the nearest familiar bucket is worse than admitting the failure is new.
description.input: One ingested failure with its context, and the library of classifications made for failures like it before.
description.core_action: Give the failure a category, a cause, a blast radius and a specific remediation, or say honestly that it is uncategorised rather than fitting it to the nearest bucket.
description.output: A classified record carrying something a person could act on, and a pattern library that classifies the next one of its kind faster.

activities.label: Read the failure with whatever context came with it
Compare it against classifications made for failures like it before
Assign category, cause and blast radius, or admit it is uncategorised
Name a specific remediation rather than a generic one
Write the classification back so the library gets better

outcomes.statement: Every ingested error gets a category, root cause, and remediation a human can act on, or an honest uncategorised needs a look rather than a forced guess.
success_criteria: Confident classifications proceed without a review gate; anything genuinely uncategorisable is flagged rather than assigned a fabricated category.
Classification history feeds the pattern library so a previously seen error type classifies faster and more confidently next time.

recipes.guidance: Own giving every ingested failure a real classification across category, cause, impact and remediation, building on what past classifications have taught about recurring patterns. When a match is genuinely ambiguous, assign the highest severity plausible category and record the ambiguity rather than hiding the uncertainty. An error type never seen before is uncategorised and needing a look, not a forced fit into an existing bucket.

recommended_trigger.rationale: A classification exists only in response to one ingested failure, so this work wakes per arrival. It is the second stage of a pipeline rather than something that chooses its own moment.

personalization_needs: What categories mean in this operation, because a taxonomy nobody uses is worse than none
What counts as a remediation a person here could actually apply, since the same fix is trivial in one operation and impossible in another

recipes.title: Cross-workflow error pattern detection

description.need: One outage arrives as a dozen unrelated looking alerts across a dozen agents, and whoever is on call spends the first stretch working out that it is one thing.
description.input: Classified failures over a recent window, which agents depend on which, and the state of the patterns already known to be active.
description.core_action: Recognise when separate failures are one thing, whether by repetition, by cascade, by clustering in time, or by a shared service, and decide whether an active pattern has changed enough to be worth saying again.
description.output: One alert per pattern rather than one per error, and a pattern record that suppresses repeat noise while still catching genuine spread.

activities.label: Hold classified failures over a recent window
Look for repetition, cascade, time clustering and shared service
Decide whether these separate failures are one thing
Decide whether an already active pattern has changed enough to say again
Raise one account for the pattern rather than one per error

outcomes.statement: A pattern spanning multiple agents or workflows, whether recurring, cascading, clustered, or a service wide outage, is caught as one incident, not experienced as several unrelated alerts.
success_criteria: Any pattern type crossing its threshold triggers a single alert naming the pattern, not one alert per underlying error.
The same active pattern does not re-alert unless a new agent joins it, so on call is not paged repeatedly for the same unresolved issue.

recipes.guidance: Own connecting individually classified failures into the systemic patterns they are actually part of, so on call sees one incident instead of a flood of unrelated looking alerts. Track pattern state, such as active or resolved and first and last seen, so dedup can suppress repeat noise while still catching genuine escalation when a new agent joins a pattern. When the channel is down, buffer and send a consolidated summary on recovery rather than losing the alerts.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Pattern detection is the third stage of a pipeline and runs against each newly classified failure, because a pattern is only worth raising while it is still forming.

personalization_needs: Which agents depend on which, because a cascade cannot be recognised without that map and it is not derivable from the failures alone
How many repetitions count as a pattern here, since that threshold is the difference between early warning and noise
What severity is worth interrupting a person for, as opposed to waiting for the periodic report

input_schema.name: recurring_threshold

description.need: Whether a fleet of agents is getting more or less reliable is usually a feeling formed from whichever incident was most recent, which is exactly the wrong basis for deciding what to fix.
description.input: The error record over the reporting window and the same measures for the preceding window.
description.core_action: Turn the record into per agent error rate and time to resolution with movement against the previous window, and rank the recommendations rather than listing the errors.
description.output: A short account of current state and a longer one of trend, with an abbreviated version stated as abbreviated when the window is too thin to support the full one.

activities.label: Aggregate the error record over the window
Compute per agent error rate and time to resolution
Compare against the preceding window for direction
Rank recommendations rather than listing errors
Publish, saying plainly when the window was too thin for the full account

success_criteria: The report states error rate and mean time to resolution per agent with movement against the previous window.
Recommendations are ranked, not just a raw error list.

recipes.title: Codebase improvement backlog scan

description.need: The work a codebase most needs is written down inside it, in markers, hotspots and deprecated calls that nobody reads, and it never reaches the place where work is chosen.
description.input: The codebase itself, whatever portfolio level health and risk signals exist for it, and the record of which kinds of candidate this operator has already rejected.
description.core_action: Decide what is genuinely worth fixing and describe each one well enough that a person can accept or reject it in seconds, without implementing anything.

recipes.title: Codebase latent defect hunt

description.need: The defects a careful reader would catch are found by users instead, because nobody has the time to read the code the way a reviewer would.
description.input: The codebase, the areas that have changed without being read, and the stable signatures of findings already filed.
description.core_action: Read like a reviewer and judge which of the things that look wrong are genuinely likely to break, filing few and real rather than many and speculative.

activities.label: Pick an area changed since it was last read
Read it the way a reviewer would, for failure paths and assumed away edges
Decide which of these would genuinely break rather than merely look unusual
Drop anything already filed under a known signature
File each surviving finding for a person to confirm

outcomes.statement: Defects that a careful reader would catch are found before a user does.
success_criteria: Each filed finding names a file and line and says what goes wrong, not just that something looks unusual
The same defect is never filed twice across passes
The proportion of filed findings a human confirms stays high enough that the queue is worth reading

recipes.guidance: Read the codebase the way a reviewer would and file what is genuinely likely to break: unhandled failure paths, missing null checks, leaked resources, edge cases the code assumes away. The accountability is signal, not volume, so a quiet pass with two real findings beats twenty speculative ones. Confirmable findings go to human triage. Escalate anything that looks like a security exposure rather than filing it in the ordinary queue.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Act when an area has changed without being read, or when the review queue has drained enough that new findings will actually be looked at. The v2 daily cron was offset from a sibling scan, which is scheduling around another job rather than around the work.

recipes.title: Codebase test coverage advance

description.need: The parts of a codebase that would hurt most if they broke are usually the parts nobody got round to testing, and a coverage percentage says nothing about which parts those are.
description.input: The codebase, the per module coverage state recorded on earlier passes, and the test conventions each module already uses.
description.core_action: Pick the next area actually worth covering rather than the one that moves the percentage most, write tests in the conventions already present, and prove they pass.
description.output: New tests that run green on the project's own runner, and a coverage state that lets the next pass resume rather than re-derive.

activities.label: Read the coverage state left by earlier passes
Choose the next area worth covering, not the one that moves the number most
Write tests in the conventions that module already uses
Run them on the project's own runner and never claim coverage unrun
Record what was covered and what remains pending

outcomes.statement: The parts of the codebase that would hurt most if they broke are the parts that have tests.
success_criteria: Every module this work has visited carries a recorded coverage state, so an unvisited area is distinguishable from a deliberately skipped one
Tests written here pass on the project's own runner before they are offered, and follow the conventions already present in that project's test files
Coverage on the areas that change most often does not fall between passes

recipes.guidance: Own the gap between what the code does and what the tests prove. Judgment here is about picking the next area worth covering, not about maximising a percentage: a thin test on a hot path beats full coverage of a config file. Follow the project's existing test conventions rather than importing your own. Never claim coverage you have not run. Escalate when a module cannot be tested without a design change.

recommended_trigger.rationale: Watch what has changed since the last pass and what is still uncovered. Act when a meaningful amount of untested code has landed, or when a previously covered area drifted; a daily cron against a quiet week writes tests nobody needed.

personalization_needs: Which codebase this work is accountable for, and which parts of it the adopter considers load bearing
What the adopter treats as an acceptable coverage bar, and whether that bar is per area rather than global
Whether new tests may land directly or must be offered for review first

description.core_action: Run the tool faithfully and turn its output into work one finding at a time, without scoring or summarising past what it actually found, and learn which unreferenced code is deliberate.
description.output: One backlog item per real finding with file and line and a concrete removal, nothing filed twice, and a plain statement when the tool could not run or its output could not be parsed.

activities.label: Run the project's configured analysis tool as the project invokes it
Parse its machine readable output without editorialising on top
Drop findings already open or already accepted as intentional
File each surviving finding with its file, line and concrete removal

outcomes.statement: Code nobody calls and code copied one time too many are found and removed rather than maintained forever.
success_criteria: Each finding carries a file and a line and a concrete removal, not a score
A finding already open is not filed again on the next sweep
Findings that turn out to be intentional are remembered as such and not re-raised

outcomes.statement: The structure the project says it has is the structure it actually has.
success_criteria: Each violation names the import or reference that crosses the line it should not
A boundary the project has deliberately relaxed stops being reported once that is known
Violations are reported as they appear rather than accumulating into an unreadable pile

recipes.guidance: Run the analysis this project's stack supports and turn its output into work, one finding at a time. The value is that the result is deterministic, so resist the urge to score, rank or summarise beyond what the tool actually found. Some dead code is deliberate and some boundary crossings were chosen on purpose, so learn which and stop raising them. Escalate rather than filing when the output suggests the configuration is wrong rather than the code.

Whether findings go straight to the backlog or through a person first

recipes.title: Codebase security scan

description.need: A generic vulnerability list is read once and ignored afterwards, because it names problems without naming what to do about them or which ones actually matter here.
description.input: The codebase and its dependency manifests, and the signatures of findings already reported on earlier scans.
description.core_action: Treat dependency vulnerabilities, exposed secrets and risky code patterns as three genuinely different questions, and rank what is found by real severity with a fix a developer could apply without further research.
description.output: Severity ranked findings each carrying a concrete remediation, deduplicated against earlier scans, with any part of the scan that could not run named as uncovered.

activities.label: Check the dependency manifests for known vulnerabilities
Search the tree for credentials that should not be in it
Read for risky patterns such as auth bypass, injection and mishandled personal data
Rank by what each would actually cost if exploited
Report each with a concrete fix, and name whatever could not be covered

outcomes.statement: Every finding tells the developer exactly what is wrong and how to fix it, ranked by real severity, not a generic vulnerability list.
success_criteria: Each finding carries a severity rank and a concrete remediation, not just a description
The same finding is not re-reported scan after scan once already surfaced

recipes.guidance: Rank by real severity and give a concrete fix, not just a description of the problem; a developer should be able to act on a finding without further research. Treat dependency vulnerabilities, exposed secrets, and risky patterns such as auth bypasses, mishandled personal data and injection as genuinely distinct categories rather than one list. Deduplicate against what has already been reported, and say which part of the scan could not run rather than letting its silence read as clean.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The v2 recipe was manual with a note that it could be scheduled or wired post merge. Look when code that handles credentials, input or personal data has changed, or when the dependency manifests have moved, rather than on a calendar that has no relationship to exposure.

Which findings the adopter has already accepted as risk, so they are not re-raised every scan
Where a serious finding should go, since a security finding in an ordinary backlog queue is a finding nobody reads in time

description.need: Structural problems cost the most and announce themselves the least, and by the time an eroded boundary or an unowned subsystem is obvious it is an incident rather than a proposal.
description.input: The codebase, the subsystems already read and when, the decisions this project has already settled, and the ideas already proposed with their outcomes.
description.core_action: Read for the structural problems that will cost most later and decide which few are worth competing with product work, treating settled decisions as constraints rather than as things to reopen.

activities.label: Read which subsystems have been analysed and what was settled before
Read a subsystem for eroded boundaries, over copied patterns and unowned code
Decide which few are worth competing with product work
Write each as an idea naming the code that motivates it, scoped to be startable
Extend the decision record so the next review does not re-derive it

success_criteria: Each idea names the code that motivates it, so a reader can check the premise without trusting the proposer
An idea is not proposed twice, and an idea already settled against is not re-proposed without new evidence
Ideas are scoped small enough that someone could start one, not framed as a rewrite

outcomes.statement: The architectural decision history is kept current, with each review building on the last instead of restating it.
success_criteria: Each review produces a record of context, decision and consequences plus a sized task breakdown.
A prior decision's settled points are referenced, not re-derived, in the next review.

recipes.guidance: Read the codebase for the structural problems that will cost the most later: boundaries that have eroded, a pattern copied past the point of usefulness, a subsystem nothing owns. Turn each into an idea with the evidence attached. Judgment is in restraint, because architecture work competes with product work and only the ideas worth that trade belong in the backlog. Settled decisions are constraints, not starting points to reopen.

How much structural work the adopter wants in the queue relative to product work
